body: Life insurers earn the margin embedded in each policy sold, measured as VNB, plus the unwind of their embedded value. Protection and non-par savings carry the highest margins, ULIPs the lowest. General insurers earn underwriting result plus investment float. Key metrics for life: APE growth, VNB margin, VNB growth, persistency (13th/61st month), product mix, EV growth and operating RoEV, banca concentration. For general: combined ratio, loss ratio, solvency and market share. Cycle drivers: equity markets (ULIP demand), interest rates (non-par pricing), tax changes (Feb 2023 Budget taxed policies above ₹5 lakh premium), IRDAI rules (surrender-value norms from Oct 2024, commission caps) and GST (individual life and health exempted from Sep 2025, losing input tax credit). Lead indicators: monthly IRDAI/Life Council new business premium, GI Council monthly premium data, bancassurance partner growth. Winners built proprietary distribution plus a diversified bank partner, balanced their product mix and kept persistency high. Losers depended on one bank partner, chased ULIP volumes in bull markets, or were LIC losing share. Valuation: P/EV. Private life insurers listed in 2016–17 at roughly 3–5x EV, de-rated to about 2–3x after the 2023 tax change. GIs trade on P/E or P/B. Nov 2026: H1 FY27 VNB is growing (ICICI Pru +22.3%, HDFC Life +12%, Bajaj Life margin 19.2%), but the GST ITC loss costs ~60–100 bps of margin. Traps: APE growth without VNB, and the GST and surrender-rule effects on reported margins.

data.business_model: Life: present value of future profits per policy (VNB) + EV unwind. General: underwriting + float income.
data.current_state_nov_2026: H1 FY27: ICICI Pru Life VNB +22.3% to ₹12.83 bn; HDFC Life VNB +12% with Q1 margin 25% (~60 bps residual GST hit); Bajaj Life H1 margin 19.2% (21.6% pre-₹95 cr GST impact). The GST exemption on individual policies (Sep 2025) helps volumes but removes ITC.
data.cycle_drivers: Equity market (ULIP), rate cycle (non-par guarantees), tax policy on maturity proceeds, IRDAI product and commission rules, GST changes.
lead_indicators: Life Insurance Council / IRDAI monthly new business premium
GI Council monthly gross direct premium
traps: Bank parent cross-sell that reverses (mis-selling crackdowns)
data.valuation: P/EV (and implied value of new business multiple). Private life 3–5x EV at the 2017–21 peak, ~2–3x after the Feb 2023 tax change. LIC listed May 2022 at ~1.1x EV and fell well below it. GIs ~25–40x P/E.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Manufacturer -> distribution (banca ~50–65% for bank-owned insurers, agency, brokers, online) -> reinsurance. Distribution captures large commissions; protection margins are highest; reinsurers set term-pricing terms.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: multi-channel distribution, protection-heavy mix, top-quartile persistency, conservative assumptions (low EV variance). Losers: single banca dependency, ULIP-heavy in a falling market, frequent negative EV assumption changes.

title: Sector playbook: Indian life and general insurance
